title: Clerical Officer/Receptionist
description: In Outpatient Administration, we place staff health and wellbeing at the heart of everything we do and actively promote flexibility in the workplace. We are committed to supporting all staff to succeed in their roles, including offering and supporting reasonable adjustments where needed. We value and recognise the power of the staff voice and encourage colleagues to act as champions through a range of staff networks, including Disability, LGBT+ and BME networks. We also adopt inclusive recruitment processes and as part of this, we share interview questions with all shortlisted candidates the day before interview. We believe this approach creates a level playing field, helps reduce stress, and enables candidates to fully understand what we are looking for. Our team is unique because we support Outpatient services across several locations and work in partnership with a wide range of Clinical Service Units. This provides a varied working environment, opportunities to develop a wide skill set, and valuable exposure to different specialties, services and different ways of working across the Trust. It is an exciting time within the Outpatient Administration team as we introduce more digital ways of working and support the Trusts commitment to sustainability by reducing paper use. If you are passionate about making a difference and want to deliver patient-centred care whilst working within a diverse and supportive team this could be the role for you! The Outpatient Administration team work in collaboration with the Referral and Booking Service, Outpatient Nursing, Switchboard, Phlebotomy and the Robotic Process Automation teams. Together we form the Outpatient Clinical Service Unit. The Outpatient Administration team are based across five sites Leeds General Infirmary, Chapel Allerton Hospital, Seacroft Hospital, Wharfedale Hospital and St James University Hospital; and two Community Diagnostic Centres at Beeston and Armley. The main duty of this role is to provide administration support to the Outpatient clinics at Wharfedale Hospital. The administration support includes computer-based work using our Patient Administration System and providing front of house reception support, delivering a high standard of patient care. Our Clerical Officer team ensure all paperwork and systems are prepared in advance of Outpatient appointments. They also provide receptionist support across a number of reception areas; book patient appointments in person and by telephone; and ensure all post clinic actions are completely timely. The main attributes we are looking for include being motivated, reliable, trustworthy, flexible, and keen to learn. We are also seeking somebody who is a good team player, with the ability to work on their own initiative. We are proud of the diversity within our teams, welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and are committed to recruiting inclusively. For questions about this job, contact: Name Natalie Hearson Position Supervisor Email n.hearson@nhs.net Phone number 0113-3921664 Shortlisting Date: 20/11/26 Interview Date: TBC Please Note: All salaries listed reflect the pay for full time roles. Any part time roles will be pro rata. What you will bring to the role Literacy and numeracy skills required for accurate record-keeping, appointment management and receptionist duties. A commitment to undertake mandatory and role-specific training as required, including additional training to meet service changes and developments. A clear insight into the duties and responsibilities of the post, demonstrating a thorough understanding of the role and the impact it has on patient experience and the wider service. Self-motivation and a commitment to provide an efficient, high-quality service in a busy and demanding environment. Reliability and dependability with a consistent approach to attendance, timekeeping and work responsibilities. A flexible and adaptable approach to duties and working practices, responding efficiently and positively to changing service needs. Competent keyboard skills with the ability to complete work accurately and efficiently to maintain a high-quality service. Good interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate politely, clearly and sensitively with patients, visitors and colleagues. An ability to work independently using own initiative and judgement, within established Trust policies, procedures and guidelines. An ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team to deliver high quality patient centred services.

title: Receptionist
description: We are a busy GP Surgery and due to an ever increasing list size and the relocation of one our receptionists we are looking to recruit a highly motivated, professional individual with excellent Customer Service Skills to join our friendly team. We are looking for full time or part time . If part time we are looking for afternoon cover till 6/6:30p.m. The role includes dealing with our patients over the telephone and face to face, undertaking administrative tasks, prescriptions and many other tasks that support our patients and the clinicians. Experience would be beneficial, however not essential. We are looking for a professional, highly motivated individual with excellent customer service and communication skills. Someone who is willing to work as part of a team and can also work on their own initiative. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Job responsibilities: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the visit book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to duty doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, either on the computer or manually. Prepare lists and notes for all surgeries and clinics held, ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Patient notes and correspondence: Make and serve refreshments, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the Partners or the practice manager. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist
description: As a key member of the Patient Services team you will be responsible for providing an efficient reception function that includes some specific administration duties. To ensure the front of house service of meeting and greeting is welcoming and portrays our standards of high quality, professional and patient-focused care. To ensure a high focus on customer satisfaction by dealing with queries in a speedy and accurate manner, applying emotionally conscious responses as relevant. To deal with patients and visitors in a courteous manner, using your skills to ensure matters are dealt with efficiently; providing effective management to patient demand, and reducing undue delay or queues at the front desk/phones To work to protocols with regard booking appointments, repeat prescriptions, ordering of patient transport including emergency ambulances and all other duties as explained to you by the Patient Services Manager. To deal with general queries and liaise effectively with clinicians and other staff as required. To support clinicians during their clinics by dealing with their queries and tasks as requested. This may be the need for some stock in their rooms, following up an appointment with the hospital, or other ad hoc requests. To provide chaperoning service where requested by the clinician and/or patient. To ensure patient confidentiality, including the use of the computer system and visibility of the screen as well as the transfer of written and verbal communication. To converse with patients and visitors by speaking clearly, precisely and with confidence both over the phone and face-to-face at the desk. To signpost patients to the most appropriate service.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Are you looking for a rewarding role where you can make a real difference to people's lives every day? As the first point of contact for patients, our reception team plays a vital role in ensuring that every patient receives a positive experience when accessing healthcare. This is a varied and challenging position that would suit someone who is: Friendly, professional, and approachable Empathetic and understanding when dealing with patients Calm and resilient in a busy environment A confident problem solver Organised and able to prioritise tasks effectively Reliable, motivated, and committed to delivering excellent customer service A team player with a positive outlook Previous reception or customer service experience is desirable, and experience within a healthcare setting would be an advantage, although full training will be provided for the right candidate. In return, we offer the opportunity to work within a close-knit, supportive team where your contribution is valued and where you can make a genuine difference to the health and wellbeing of our patients. If you would like to join a practice that takes pride in caring for both its patients and staff, we would love to hear from you. Greeting patients and visitors in a professional, friendly and helpful manner. Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments. Signposting patients to the most appropriate service or healthcare professional. Processing prescription requests in line with practice procedures. Managing incoming and outgoing correspondence, including emails, letters and clinical documents. Registering new patients and maintaining accurate patient records. Scanning, coding and filing patient information using clinical computer systems. Liaising with GPs, nurses, hospitals and other healthcare providers. Supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Maintaining patient confidentiality and complying with information governance requirements. Undertaking other administrative tasks as required by the practice. General Reception Duties A1. To work at the Reception Desk, greeting patients on arrival in a polite, welcoming manner. A2. To handle patient request for appointments and medication in a helpful, efficient way. A3. To answer the telephone promptly with a suitable greeting. A4. To deal with difficult, demanding patients on the phone in an appropriate manner and record telephone calls as appropriate when issues arise. A5. To ensure all messages are dealt with efficiently and appropriately making sure a contact telephone number is taken and then passed on to the relevant person(s) in an efficient and timely manner. A6. To ensure phone calls are transferred appropriately and efficiently to relevant members of staff ensuring that clinicians are free before doing so. A7. To ensuring requests from other parties (solicitors, other NHS agencies etc) are carried out within the confidentiality guidelines of the Data Protection Act (Information Governance Training will be given appropriately) and accurate records are kept of such communications as necessary. A8. To ensure online consultations requests are responded to and processed in a timely fashion A9. To advise patients of relevant charges for non-NHS and private services, accept payment and issue receipts for the same. A10. To inform the Practice Manager if a patient raises a concern or complaint with written details of the incident. A11. To complete patients request for repeat prescription items accurately and send through to the GP to sign. A12. To ensure that any items requested from the patient or patients carer that are not on the repeated items screen must requested from the Pharmacist Group detailing items requested and why they are requesting medication. A13. To deal with requests from the clinicians for patient contact or recall in an efficient timely manner. A14. To take requests from members of the public wishing to become patients issuing the appropriate information and application form and advising them of the new patient application process adopted here. A15. To ensure that all temporary patients and requests for immediate necessary treatment complete the required forms and are registered onto the system before their appointment. A16. To ensure that all New Baby registrations requests have the relevant forms completed and registered onto the system in a timely fashion. A17. To take responsibility that the signed prescription box is not accessible to the general public if ever the reception desk is left unmanned. A18. To ensure that any paper prescriptions are only collected by patients, authorised family members or pharmacies. A19. To take responsibility for all patient samples handed over the reception desk, ensuring that they have the patients details and that they are correct and are passed on to the appropriate nurse or entered into the colour coded plastic bags ready to be taken to the path labs at HRI. A20. To receive internal and external mail and deal with it appropriately, distributed to relevant trays or scanning onto the system and forwarded electronically. No items marked Private and Confidential should be opened by anyone but the intended recipient or their delegate ie, the Practice Manager will open this for the for GP when he is on leave. A21. All incoming post must be dealt with in an efficient and timely manner. A22. To input data as directed by GP, accurately and in a timely fashion onto the patients electronic record, relevant to shift worked. A23. To ensure relevant information is passed on as required for the next shift. These duties are performed by the receptionists as a team and therefore you should be able to take the initiative and perform these duties as and when required. B1. Depending on rota, to open up the surgery premises at the start of day, resetting alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. B2. Depending on rota, secure the surgery premises at end of day, ensuring all fires/heaters are switched off, all doors and windows are closed & locked, surgery is totally secured, internal lights off and alarm activated. B3. To ensure external mail is posted or taken to the post office in a timely fashion. B4. To partake in the performing of processing referral letters/medical reports/supporting letters. B5. To partake in photocopying relevant to office duties (Solicitors requests from patient files, X-ray forms and any other forms required as hand outs). B6. To ensure that the appropriate details are taken and noted accurately on the visit screen when a home visit is requested. A brief summary printout and blank prescription should also be attached and placed in the visit box in a timely manner. B7. To ensure reception and waiting areas are kept neat, tidy and safe. B8. To ensure that, after use, the patient notes are accurately filed in the correct filing system, ie alphabetical order Surname, First Name. B9. To ensure all paper waste which may contain confidential information, no longer needed, relating to the surgery or a patient is put in the shredding bins as a means of disposal. B10. To take responsibility/sign for any items deliver to the practice, ensuring that they are passed onto the intended recipient or placed in the intended area, i.e. fridge immediately. B11. To receive internal and external mail and deal with it appropriately, distributed to relevant trays or scanning onto the system and forwarded electronically. No items marked Private and Confidential should be opened by anyone but the intended recipient or their delegate ie, the Practice Manager will open this for the for GP when he is on leave. B12. To act as a chaperone when requested by a clinician for an examination and ensure a record is made of your presence on the patients record. B13. Review and process incoming emails and voicemails received in the generic email inbox. Miscellaneous C1. To be prepared to offer assistance as and when necessary due to staff shortages or to an increased workload. C2. To make every effort to attend practice meetings and training arranged by the practice even if this is outside the normal hours of work. Appropriate notice will be given and time in lieu awarded. C3. To ensure an active part is taken with the general duties of maintaining running a smooth office environment. C4. To be proactive in seeking to acquire new skills which will be to the benefit of the Practice and the role employed by the practice, such as any training courses, reading etc. C5. To follow any guidance given and adhere to the Practice Protocols written by the Doctor, Nurse and Practice Manager. C6. To take responsibility at all times for the health and safety of oneself, fellow employees and patients. C7. To be aware and comply with the practices Health & Safety Policies C8. To be aware of fire procedures, how to raise the alarm, fire fighting equipment and its use, the fire evacuation procedure and your responsibilities in an emergency situation to both patients and fellow staff members. C9. To be aware of the Practice First Aid procedures and ensure the accident book is appropriately completed as necessary. C10. To be aware of the constraints of confidentiality and in particular the Data Protection Act 2018 and its relevance to you both in, and outside of work. C11. To be aware of the Good Practice Guidelines for General Practice Electronic Records and the information contained relevant to your role. C12. To be aware of the contents of the Practice IT policies and Procedures File comply with their direction regarding the use of IT within the practice. C13. To be aware of the contents of the Practice HR policies and comply with their direction. C14. To always act within the best interest of the practice, patients and employees. C15. To support the GPs, Practice Nurses, Practice Manager and all fellow employees at all times. C16. To ensure that any other (appropriate) tasks are performed as requested by the Doctor or Practice Manager taking capacity and training into consideration.

title: Medical receptionist
description: We are recruiting for a medical receptionist to join our friendly and busy team. This role provides reception and administrative support to the whole practice. Customer service experience and IT skills are essential. A knowledge of primary care and the IT system (System One) would be an advantage but not essential as training is provided. Good written and oral communication skills are also essential as well as good time management and organisational skills to prioritise your workload, along with an understand of, and commitment to, patient confidentiality. Welcoming patients to the surgery and providing a friendly and professional reception service.Answering incoming telephone calls promptly and dealing with a wide range of patient queries. Booking, cancelling and rearranging GP, nurse and other clinical appointments. Supporting patients with general enquiries and directing them to the appropriate service. Take accurate messages and relaying information to the relevant team members. Managing the reception area and assisting patients with check-in and other administrative queries. Liaising with GPs, nurses, administrative staff and other healthcare professionals. Maintaining accurate and confidential patient records. Handling sensitive and sometimes challenging conversations calmly, respectfully and professionally. Following practice procedures relating to confidentiality, safeguarding, information governance and patient care. Carrying out general administrative duties to support the smooth running of the practice. Please see receptionist job description attached to this advert in supporting documents. title: Patient Services Administrator
description: At Northgate Surgery, our Patient Service Administrators play a vital role in supporting the smooth and effective delivery of primary care services. Working alongside our Patient Service Advisors, GPs, nurses, management team, and external healthcare providers, you will be responsible for a wide range of administrative duties that directly contribute to patient care and the efficient running of the practice. This is a varied and rewarding role suited to an organised, detail-focused individual who enjoys working in a busy healthcare environment. The successful candidate will support key administrative functions including the processing of medical reports, private work, patient records management, prescription administration, clinical correspondence, and results enquiries. The hours for this role are Monday,Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 9-5 and Wednesdays 8:30-4 The successful candidate will be responsible for: Processing and coordinating Insurance, GP Reports (IGPR), Subject Access Requests, and other medical report requests. Administering private work requests, including private letters, medical examinations, insurance documentation, and associated invoicing. Managing prescription-related queries in accordance with practice procedures and policies. Processing and responding to patient and healthcare professional test results enquiries in line with practice protocols. Scanning, coding, and processing incoming correspondence and clinical documentation. Maintaining accurate electronic patient records and ensuring information is updated appropriately. Supporting the summarisation and management of patient medical records. Monitoring and managing clinical administration workflows and shared practice inboxes. Liaising with hospitals, pharmacies, community services, and other healthcare organisations regarding administrative matters. Producing routine correspondence, reports, and documentation as required. Supporting quality improvement initiatives, enhanced services, and contractual requirements. Maintaining confidentiality and ensuring compliance with GDPR, Information Governance, and practice policies. Working collaboratively with colleagues across the practice to ensure administrative work is completed accurately and within agreed timescales.

title: Ward Clerk

title: GP Receptionist / Care Navigator
description: We are recruiting for a Care Navigator to join our team. The role will be part time, and you must be available to work Friday evenings up until 18:30pm. Working within the Robin Lane reception team, the post-holder will help provide a friendly and welcoming service for all patients. The Care Navigator will support patients to access the right health care in a professional and efficient manner. Follow practice processes to actively signpost patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional and service, whilst handling any complex queries and challenging situations in a professional manner, ensuring any issues are resolved where possible, at the first point of contact. To welcome patients presenting either in person or by telephone; ensuring you respond promptly and positively. Book appointments for patients and cancel appointments where needed. Support patients in navigating to the most appropriate service, which may include informing patients of external health care providers and online services. Effectively handle all queries that present at the practice; problem solving, signposting and escalation of matters, as appropriate. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare providers. Treat all patients fairly and with respect. Provide cover across all sites as required. This is not an exhaustive list, and it is expected that this role will develop as the business grows.

Coding Identify relevant clinical information contained in patient correspondence Code or free text the clinical information on to the patient record Deal with queries relating to coding Appointments Process appointment requests for today and future appointments from patients by telephone and in person. Telephone Have working knowledge of telephone system, during and after hours. Other Tasks Ensure building security have thorough knowledge of doors/windows/alarm. Any other tasks allocated by the Partners or Practice Manager. Confidentiality : In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety : The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines. Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Equality and Diversity : The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a manner, which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development : Mandatory training courses, i.e. fire safety, safeguarding, CPR etc. Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members, patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services : The post-holder will: Work in accordance with practice policies, standards and guidance. Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work. Make use of information technology systems available within the Practice, following systems for data security and protection. Participate in audit where appropriate. Attend and participate in practice meetings/training events. Any other duties commensurate with the role to ensure the smooth running of the Practice. This job description may need to be reviewed as the Practice develops.

title: Care Navigator/ Medical Receptionist
description: South Queen Street Medical Centre are looking to appoint a care navigator/ receptionist to join our busy GP practice who will be the first point of contact for patients, contractors, and visitors as well as carrying out general office management tasks. Working pattern 5 hours per day, 5 days a week, alternate weekly am & pm shifts, 8am-630pm. Flexibility and overtime will be required for this role. You will be responsible for the general reception duties within the Practice and work with our established processes, policies, and procedures to provide a comprehensive high-quality service and deal efficiently and courteously with patient enquiries. You will receive, assist, and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. You will provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. You will have excellent communication skills, a compassionate and friendly nature who can operate in a busy environment with a range of people and professions, as you will be working with our clinical and administration teams. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organised and an effective communicator who can provide a professional and warm welcome to our patients, ensuring every contact is of the highest quality. IT skills are essential, as you will be regularly creating searches, data input and monitoring our achievements and progress against national, local, and internal targets. You will also process prescription requests and provide a full administrative service. GCSE grade C or above in English and Maths is essential for this role. Key Duties and Responsibilities Patient Reception and Customer Service Act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Welcome patients in a friendly, respectful and professional manner. Respond to general enquiries and provide accurate information about practice services, opening hours and appointment procedures. Deal sensitively with patients who may be anxious, distressed, frustrated or experiencing difficult personal circumstances. Maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception and waiting area. Manage challenging situations professionally and escalate complaints or concerns to the appropriate member of the practice team. Care Navigation and Appointment Management Handle patient requests for appointments, advice and access to healthcare services by telephone and in person. Use approved care navigation protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician or service, including GPs, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, physiotherapists and other available services where appropriate. Gather relevant non-clinical information to help determine the appropriate appointment pathway, without attempting to diagnose medical conditions. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the practices clinical computer system. Identify potentially urgent concerns in accordance with practice procedures and promptly escalate them to a clinician. Provide information about alternative services, such as NHS 111, where appropriate and in accordance with practice guidance. Maintain accurate records of patient contacts and appointment requests. Telephone and Administrative Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and manage a busy call queue efficiently. Handle patient messages and ensure they are passed to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies and direct medication queries to the appropriate professional. Register new patients and update demographic details, contact information and other relevant records. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and electronic communications. Assist with administrative tasks, including recalling patients for appointments, supporting clinical audits and maintaining accurate practice records. Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow up requests within agreed timescales. Clinical Systems and Data Management Use the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, to access and update patient information. Ensure patient details, appointment information and messages are recorded accurately and promptly. Handle sensitive patient information securely and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, data protection legislation, information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures for accessing, storing and sharing patient information appropriately. Teamwork and Practice Support Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, care coordinators and administrative colleagues. Attend staff meetings and training sessions as required. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception services. Follow practice policies relating to health and safety, infection prevention, safeguarding and equality and diversity. Report incidents, risks and concerns to the appropriate manager. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role to support the effective operation of the practice. Training and Development The successful candidate will receive induction and training appropriate to the role, including practice procedures, clinical systems, information governance, confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety and care navigation. Ongoing training and development will be encouraged to support the delivery of a safe, efficient and high-quality patient service. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic, dependable and proactive. The successful candidate must demonstrate patience, discretion and professionalism when dealing with sensitive situations and be committed to treating every patient with dignity, respect and fairness. Working Conditions The postholder will work within a busy GP practice and may be required to work flexibly according to the needs of the service. Working hours, salary, annual leave and other employment terms will be confirmed during recruitment.
